# Vendor robot SDK adapters and six-language examples

The package contains an official-primary-source inventory for all nineteen named vendors, a closed DATA planner, an implemented source materialize/bind/generate pipeline, and six actual SDK-facing complete-type telemetry components. The reviewed source package is integrated under `sdk/robots/vendors`. Its inventory, preparation pipeline and six language components have passed independent source review. Native SDK acquisition, code generation, compilation, Runtime execution and robot acceptance for this package remain pending; the original Unitree profiles and historical acceptance reports retain their original status.

This is useful shared implementation, not nineteen completed vendor adapters. Each component calls the existing capability/session or typed polling APIs and requires a real complete model binding. None supplies an imaginary vendor type, native layout, default topic, default grant or hardware oracle. Model selection and SDK/firmware/RDK/FCI major remain separate from ROS major. The native SDK languages in `inventory.json` are vendor-documentation facts; the six requested languages are our Guest adapter goal, not a claim that each vendor ships all six.

## Official primary inventory

`inventory.json` has exactly nineteen unique vendors and explicit per-family source status. Every row has its own URLs, product scope, compatibility caveats, missing source/native roles and zero new acceptance counts. Default branches and documentation URLs are mutable research evidence. Each row's upstream revision/tree hash remains null until actual acquisition and review. An inventory record is never a machine-readable checkmark for execution.

The xArm `RobotMsg` [official source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xArm-Developer/xarm_ros2/humble/xarm_msgs/msg/RobotMsg.msg) illustrates the concrete closure problem: it depends on Header/time and includes dynamic joint data plus fixed arrays. A scalar-only projection or invented fixed carrier limit would not be a complete adapter. Its moving Humble URL is research evidence; an immutable revision is still missing (the official Git ref endpoint was unavailable during this read). The package does not manufacture a commit or a native hash to proceed.

## Implemented shared components

`examples/telemetry.c`, `telemetry.hpp`, `telemetry.rs`, `telemetry.mjs`, `telemetry.ts` and `telemetry.go` are real source components over existing current SDK APIs. They have not been compiled. Their common lifecycle is fresh instance, explicit ABI-compatible initialization, mode0 default-denied open or separate mode1 typed subscription, at most4096 caller-driven polls, complete decode before model observation, and explicit checked cleanup after dispatch returns. Idle11 never means delivery. Native errors and model-observer errors remain errors; there is no automatic retry, timer, thread, goroutine, network endpoint, clock permission or management import.

The components use a complete generated record/codec and a separately reviewed model observer. The observer must expose/compare the full relevant typed values against an actual independent native peer. A locally incremented count or marker alone is not evidence. Poll reentry/close during dispatch is refused; Rust additionally relies on actual safe ownership and the SDK's intrinsic dispatch guard. Traps/panics/kills remain the responsibility of the external current Runtime/process owner. Closing a handle is not module-wide ROS-authority retirement; this infrastructure adds no management operation.

C uses a stable one-slot `roswasmc_session`, real open/subscribe/poll and checked session cleanup. `vendor_binding.h` is intentionally absent: it must be made from the actual complete model-generated source, with the exact typed aliases and observer specified in `binding-contract.json`. Compilation without that binding must fail. C++ uses `roswasmcpp::Session` and the actual `Codec<Message>` specialization, with a stable borrowed owner and explicit capacity. It emits no formatting; an application choosing diagnostics can use the project's current fast_io output adapters without custom native layout casts.

Rust is generic over the actual generated `Canonical` type and uses real Session/Node/typed Executor. Build alloc and exactly one backend feature. JavaScript requires the real SDK Session over a genuine copied QuickJS-in-Wasm transport and stages the entire current SDK import closure. A host Node process, mock bridge or fabricated Memory/Instance cannot qualify it. AssemblyScript uses a source-bound backend reexport and actual Codec<T>; its concrete model callback must be noncapturing. TinyGo uses the real tagged SDK Session/Node/Executor and complete generated decoder, with an explicit reactor initializer in its actual build recipe.

These are shared library/lesson components, not ready-to-run robot applications. `binding-contract.json` lists each missing concrete entry/export/observer/stage role. Existing Unitree typed entries remain the concrete maintained reuse reference; no new vendor identity or Unitree pass count is inferred. Java and C# files are reserved for their other owner and were not inspected or changed.

## Closed source planner

`adapter_plan.plan(inventory, request, *, read)` is stdlib-only and performs no filesystem/process/network operation itself. The trusted Root caller supplies `read(role, expected_full7)` after actual selected-root/same-FD admission; the planner rechecks the returned exact byte extent/SHA. All native provenance is still a separate Root responsibility. It does not validate Git signatures or infer firmware from a repository URL.

The closed request names vendor, model, ROS major, SDK revision, exact alias/resource, native trait identity, separate canonical codec identity, source lock, actual generation receipt and every generated output. Unestablished backends are refused. The source lock must be immutable/reviewed and model/revision-associated. Every complete source dependency and catalog is read and matched to the generator's actual `source_inputs`; every generated output is read and matched to its actual output ledger. The selected complete typed record must match both identities and its finite canonical bound. Missing, partial, duplicate, unbound or merely guest-only generations are refused. The current lock variant is Git-source scoped; closed binary SDK deliveries require a separately reviewed archive/version admission before they can use it.

Even a successful planner return is `UNEXECUTED_SOURCE_PLAN_NO_AUTHORITY`, with every compile/Runtime/native/hardware boolean false. It describes one required topic.subscribe authority; it never opens it, sets rights, changes a Gateway, acquires a robot address, or treats vendor labels as principals. Host CLI policy must remain empty by default and separately bind all original byte/rate/queue/QoS/timeout/event quotas. The actual Runtime lane must prove enabled business namespace/default denial, full source/SDK/tool/native ELF/Guest mappings, original pidfd ownership and normal Frame.finish. No generic topic string is presented as full vendor support.

## Simulator command hold/stop

`simulator-hold-stop.recipe.json` is deliberately blocked pending real model command definitions, exact SDK/controller revision, simulator-only native endpoint and an independent native witness. A zero vector is not a generic hold command. Robot modes, leases, acknowledgements and stop semantics differ; neither a universal Twist nor a vendor SDK function name can substitute for the real command schema. No command is published by the six telemetry components.

The useful next implementation step is model-specific binding: generate the entire official command/telemetry family, write the actual typed hold/stop constructors in all six languages, then pace one hold and one stop with an external actual simulator controller. Default-denied and positive instances remain distinct. Unknown outcome after timeout is preserved without command replay. Hardware qualification, vendor official suites and real-time/control stability remain independent routes. `inventory.json` enumerates the exact remaining source/native roles per vendor instead of assigning invented test universes.

## VTune hardware and fast_io work

Intel's [hardware sampling documentation](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/vtune-profiler/user-guide/2023-0/hw-event-based-sampling-collection.html) describes PMU sampling and its collection prerequisites; [Microarchitecture Exploration](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/vtune-profiler/user-guide/2024-2/general-exploration-view.html) depends on actual hardware event capabilities. These cited documentation editions explain requirements; they do not identify an installed profiler version or confirm PMU access here.

Future hardware Hotspots and microarchitecture routes must record actual CPU model/PMU/perf access, exact installed VTune binary/version and options, current native process/source/symbol/map identities, result data and bounded ownership. Do not silently substitute software sampling and label it hardware. If the measured process is host QEMU, metrics describe the actual host/QEMU execution, not an unmeasured ARM microarchitecture. No sysctl, driver install, kernel permission change or profiling command is performed by this package. Existing fast_io production and fixture work remains separately reviewed; this candidate does not rewrite it or claim performance improvements.

Source parsing/hashes and API reads are the only authored evidence so far; no test, compiler or generator was run. The source-ready package binds these files, the exact current Source64 SDK support entries, the attachment and web-research URL set. Independent source review is complete; it does not count as compilation or runtime acceptance. The current Unitree/ARM boundary stays the priority; the inventory cannot replace its still-required original six routes.

## Implemented source preparation and native exporter pipeline

`vendor_prepare.prepare(inventory, request, *, read, load, out)` is an actual source implementation. It writes a fresh complete input closure, retains the original official license/lock, calls the current bounded-v2 parser and guest-only six-language generator, emits a real model-native identity exporter, and returns actual output pins. It performs no subprocess/network/robot operation. It has not been called here. `preparation.request.template.json` is deliberately null for unknown facts; it cannot be used until the caller supplies actual ordinary full7s, exact model/revision and a complete official schema/bounds/native-header inventory.

The injected `load(relative, unique_name)` must admit the entire current MF bytes before loading the three original-mode fixed repository modules, with correct temporary dataclass module registration/restoration. The implementation calls `bounded.load_catalog` and `bounded.generate` directly with the real `custom_types` parent; it never uses an ambient candidate import or custom_types' independent provider lookup. All ten original-mode fixed support bodies are admitted/reopened, including four Service/Action facade templates and the original native metadata/protocol sources. `read(role, full7)` remains the trusted caller's actual selected-root, opened-FD, mode/nlink and whole-source guard boundary; this library additionally checks returned size/SHA. The fresh output directory is caller-owned authority. A failed preparation preserves its partial source for review and does not overwrite an older revision.

The exporter retains the exact helper namespace from the current `tests/ros_custom_types/bounded-v2/native_identity.cc`. Only its include and finite type-call inventory are generated. Message/Service/Action root and every component use actual official ROS traits or type-support metadata. ROS1 Action wrapper/component conventions stay intact. Every original installed native header is a separate admitted role. This original exporter refuses ROS2 SDKs without the actual modern hash/TypeDescription API. The separately reviewed explicit legacy-introspection source mode below preserves full native comparison and derived provenance; it still requires actual SDK/process qualification and never claims an available baked hash. The emitted C++ includes the original current native protocol through an explicit repository include root and retains SIGSTOP plus one bounded `I` gate, so the future owner must prove actual ELF/maps/whole MD and native SDK/library/source closure before releasing it. No ROS Node or native endpoint is created by this identity tool.

`vendor_prepare.bind_and_generate(preparation_pin, native_metadata, native_owner_evidence, *, read, load, out)` then copies separately obtained original metadata/evidence into another fresh source directory, invokes the existing strict `bind_catalog.bind`, and invokes the real six-language/native-registry source generator. It pins every generated output and bound catalog/definition. Native-owner evidence is retained DATA, never a boolean or status string that this tool promotes into a transport qualification. Native registry **source emission** remains different from registration or rights. No native MD5/RIHS is derived by this tool. The actual generator's canonical protocol-v1 `UWVMROS1_...` prefix is shared across both ROS majors; the ROS major remains in the canonical IR and is checked separately. The planner now associates original unbound catalog → actual binding receipt → separately derived native-bound catalog → generation/output bytes; it does not incorrectly require the mutated catalog to retain the original catalog hash.

`examples/twist_telemetry.hpp` is a concrete C++ wrapper over the current complete builtin Twist codec, including its actual48-byte canonical extent. The six generic telemetry components can likewise receive their real current Twist codec/record type, listed exactly in `standard-facilities.json`. None publishes a velocity command or claims vendor hold/stop semantics. Complete JointState now has a separately authored explicit official-standard mode, with Header/JointState dependency closure and ROS1 primitive normalization. The old custom profile keeps its Header/time/standard-namespace rejection. This wiring requires the companion standard implementation in the actual current source before using that mode; native identity export, generation, compilation and delivery remain pending. No timestamp, name or optional array is renamed or discarded.

Source-only invocation contract (unexecuted):

1. Root independently qualifies/acquires the exact official package revision, complete source/license/native generated headers and any SDK/controller revision. Populate the null request with real file observations and reviewed dynamic capacities; use the original actual upstream Git lock, not a moving branch label.
2. Under a fresh owned source output, call `prepare` with full-MF `load` and actual selected-file `read`. Inspect all six codec sources and emitted native exporter before any native process.
3. In the real current ROS native SDK, compile/link the exporter with full system-inclusive MD and original libraries; prove architecture/mappings/ownership, release its mapping stop and one `I` gate, preserve raw metadata and normal owner cleanup. This native execution lane is a separately required future operation.
4. Call `bind_and_generate` on those actual original metadata/evidence pins. Inspect all generated source, then source-freeze the complete new bundle before actual SDK/Guest/Gateway compilation.
5. Bind each complete generated type/observer to the six source components. Actual compiles, Guest validation, enabled-backend/default-denied zero-effect controls, exact native value oracle, finite cleanup/revocation, simulator commands and vendor official suites are all separate required results.

`test_vendor_preparation_policy.suite(api, *, inventory, native_exporter_source)` retains the original ten authored pure-policy methods unchanged and adds nine mode/provenance methods below, for nineteen unexecuted methods. Root supplies the separately admitted external API and actual MF-bound exporter body; there is no ambient candidate import or filesystem fixture. The cases cover closed roles, traversal/injection refusal, actual ROS namespace/header categories, unchanged official metadata helpers, ROS1 Action root/components and Service-first inventory. Synthetic `policy_fixture` names are source-generation DATA, not vendor official cases, native identity proofs or delivery counts.


## Observer-error correction, preserved source successor

The original JS correction preserves its complete first held foundation in external `/tmp` evidence; no forensic copy is required inside the installed SDK tree. In JavaScript `pollOnce`, only a **normal returned** native status11 means an empty queue. A thrown codec, bridge or model-observer exception is an operation failure even when its RosError code is11: the source now calls checked cleanup, retains that primary code and retires the example. It cannot silently leave status0 and keep polling after an observer failure. The original six-language source boundaries, ten authored policy cases and all zero execution/acceptance counts remain unchanged. This is a source correction only; no JavaScript Guest, native peer or test was run.

The separately reviewed source lineage preserves the original r2 package and later mode predecessors in external `/tmp` evidence; no forensic `before-r2` directory is required inside the installed SDK tree. The preparer also accepts the exact `uwvm-ros-official-standard-bounded-v1` catalog, preserving its `registered` markers and complete original definition/header inventory. It requires the actual current-MF bounded module to expose the reviewed standard mode before creating source output. The separately reviewed maintained dispatcher/parser/binder/combine/native-registry and ROS1 Definition changes were integrated by Root under their distinct source receipt. The actual selected current source must still contain them; an old generator is refused, not relabelled. The exporter already selects exact official namespaces/includes and needs no new fake type or identity path. Binding still uses the actual strict native exporter/binder/generator and pins every generated language/native output.

The telemetry planner now binds its selected alias to an actual `.msg` catalog entry whose registration is enabled. ## Explicit older-ROS2 Message identity preparation

The optional request key `identity_mode` is omitted by historical requests and defaults to `original-native-metadata`. That branch retains the original native exporter. It never catches a modern hash failure and retries another provider. The original ROS2 binding/planning branch also refuses legacy-provenance envelopes rather than silently consuming a separately derived receipt. Only an explicit `legacy-introspection` request may use the independently reviewed `legacy_ros2_exporter` module with a complete unbound ROS2 catalog. A real modern type-support structure is always refused by its C++ compatibility helper, including missing or malformed modern hash callbacks. ROS1 cannot enter this branch. Complete Service and Action roots follow the separately documented workflows below rather than being reduced to Message payload hashes.

The preparer admits the original ten current source roles plus all eight exact `LEGACY_SUPPORT` roles in `vendor_prepare.py`. The pure emitter is loaded as the fourth actual current-MF module through the caller's `load(relative,name)` function, never ambient `sys.path`. Every support body is reopened after loading and again after source work. Compatibility metadata/digest/identity/features, original native I/O, native declarations and canonical grammar are explicit source evidence; actual SDK headers, full-MD/link and stopped-process library ownership remain additional native prerequisites.

The emitted exporter materializes all actual native introspection metadata before its owned SIGSTOP checkpoint. Only the original finite stdin `I` gate releases one at-most-16-MiB document. Preparation retains a complete native-declaration schema source sidecar using original native bounds, separately from canonical buffer quotas. Binding reparses the actual unbound definitions through the current generator, requires the schema sidecar to match, and validates every original raw metadata root/component, full declaration/reference graph, derived-provenance marker and unavailable baked-hash fact before copying an identity. No MD5 or RIHS value is calculated in Python. The original raw native exporter/owner reports, copied reports and their distinct full7 identities remain retained; a JSON success or provenance marker is not accepted as proof that a native process ran.

The source-binding receipt and planner preserve `native_identity_mode`, the exact per-Message provenance association and original/native-copy evidence. The planner reopens both actual metadata copies and declaration copies and rejects any mismatch. It still returns an unexecuted source plan with empty authority. The nine new injected policy cases are request/provenance refusals and original-mode selection checks, bringing the authored vendor suite from ten to nineteen methods; none has run. Synthetic syntax sentinels in negative cases are never bound as native identities or emitted as accepted native receipts.

Complete zero-field Topic preparation remains required implementation work. Complete Service/Action protocol/event roots now have separate source implementations below, with genuine native representation tests still required. These are not completed vendor support. The existing required ledger also retains arbitrary constants/defaults/wstring/IDL, nonfinite sensor values, large payloads and actual per-model integration work. This source-only successor establishes no distribution, architecture, native delivery, robot hardware or vendor official-test qualification.
